intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

selected_hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning coastlines along the cliffside trail connecting Praia da Marinha to Benagil. Descend to hidden grottos, golden coves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters perfect for snorkeling and swimming. The dramatic limestone formations make this a bucket-list beach experience.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden sea arches, secluded beaches, and the cathedral-like Algar de Benagil cave with its natural skylight. An unforgettable blend of adventure and natural wonder.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit boutique wineries in the Lagoa wine region, the heart of Algarve viticulture. Sample indigenous varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco paired with local cheeses and charcuterie. A knowledgeable guide walks you through the vineyards explaining the unique terroir shaped by the Mediterranean climate and sandy soils.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Sunset Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, a UNESCO-protected wetland of barrier islands, tidal flats, and diverse birdlife. Stop at the pristine Ilha Deserta for a swim and fresh seafood lunch at the island's only restaurant. Watch the golden sunset paint the lagoon as you return to Faro — a perfect blend of nature and relaxation.

experiences.name: Tavira Old Town & Local Wine Tasting Evening
experiences.description: Wander through the charming whitewashed streets of Tavira, one of the Algarve's most authentic towns, visiting the Roman bridge, Moorish castle ruins, and ornate churches. End the evening at a traditional tasca for a curated tasting of regional Alentejo and Algarve wines paired with petiscos (Portuguese tapas) like bacalhau croquettes and presunto.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, clear customs, and arrange transfer to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (approx. 1h drive from Faro Airport via A22; budget tip: take the Eva Bus from Faro to Lagoa/Carvoeiro for ~€5 instead of a taxi).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in, freshen up, then take a short 10-minute walk to Praia da Marinha — consistently rated one of Portugal's most beautiful beaches. Explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea arches, and crystal-clear water. No entrance fee. Swim or simply relax and recover from the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the village of Lagoa or nearby Carvoeiro (5 km, reachable by local bus or taxi share) for a casual first dinner. Explore the small waterfront promenade of Carvoeiro.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a pastel de nata and coffee at Faro Airport café (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bifana (pork sandwich) or tosta mista at a café near the bus station in Lagoa (~€3–4)
meals.dinner: O Castelo restaurant in Carvoeiro or A Fonte in Lagoa — look for the 'prato do dia' (dish of the day) which typically includes soup, main, and drink for ~€8–10

day_by_day.notes: Eva Bus line from Faro to Lagoa runs regularly. A taxi costs ~€45–55. Pre-book a seat if traveling with luggage. September weather in Algarve is warm (24–28°C) with minimal rain — perfect beach conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Praia da Marinha before crowds arrive. Pack a picnic breakfast and watch the sunrise over the cliffs. Walk the coastal cliff trail eastward toward Praia do Carvalho — a hidden beach accessible through a tunnel carved in the rock. Free entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Lagoa town center (5 km by local bus ~€1.50) and visit the Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa — one of the Algarve's most historic wine cooperatives. Free or very low-cost tastings of local Algarve wines including Negra Mole and Crato Branco varieties. Pick up a bottle of local wine for ~€4–6.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Carvoeiro village. Walk the short boardwalk to Algar Seco rock formations at sunset — dramatic carved limestone sea stacks, free to visit. Dinner back in Carvoeiro.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered picnic: buy fresh bread, local cheese, and fruit from Lagoa market or Pingo Doce supermarket (~€3–4 total)
meals.lunch: Light snack at a pastelaria in Lagoa town — soup and bread (~€3)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Barco in Carvoeiro — grilled fish 'peixe grelhado' with salad and potatoes (~€10–13). Ask for the daily fish special.

day_by_day.notes: Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa is open weekdays; confirm hours before visiting. Algar Seco is a 15-minute walk from Carvoeiro center. Bring water and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Take the local bus west toward Portimão (20 min, ~€2). Visit the Museu de Portimão — an award-winning museum housed in a former sardine canning factory. Entry is free on Sunday mornings but only €3 on other days. Excellent insight into Algarve fishing history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across the bridge to Ferragudo — a charming, less-touristy fishing village with a castle (Castelo de São João do Arade, exterior view free) and colorful boats. Explore the narrow whitewashed streets. Swim at Praia de Ferragudo, a long sandy beach with calm waters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a bar overlooking the Arade River estuary in Ferragudo. Bus back to Lagoa/Carvoeiro area.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and croissant at a local café near the hotel (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Tasca do Rato in Ferragudo — local tasca-style lunch with fresh seafood, prato do dia ~€8–9
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner: buy fresh sardines from Portimão market or Pingo Doce, grill at accommodation if facilities available, pair with your Lagoa wine (~€5–6 total)

day_by_day.notes: Portimão is a major hub with good bus connections. The Portimão market (Mercado Municipal) is worth a quick browse for fresh produce and local goods.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — the medieval Moorish capital of the Algarve. Take the bus from Lagoa (15 min, ~€1.50). Visit the impressive red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves) — entry €2.80 with EU student card or €2.80 standard. Panoramic views over orange groves and the Arade River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves Cathedral (Sé de Silves, free entry), the old Moorish walls, and the charming cobblestone streets. Visit the Museu Arqueológico de Silves (€2.10). Walk along the riverfront and browse local shops for affordable ceramics and cork products.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa area. Friday evening in Lagoa town — locals gather at the main square. Enjoy the relaxed atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Café Inglês in Silves (arrive early) or eat before departure — coffee and pastel de nata (~€2)
meals.lunch: Café Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — famous for cataplana (seafood stew), but opt for the affordable grilled chicken or pork with fries ~€8–10
meals.dinner: Tasca in Lagoa town — look for a local restaurant away from the tourist strip. Bifanas, caldo verde soup, and local wine ~€7–9

day_by_day.notes: Silves is an unmissable historical gem. September is still warm but less crowded than summer. The Silves Medieval Fair happens in August, so September is quieter and more authentic.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos) — one of Portugal's most scenic coastal walks. Start from Praia da Marinha and walk west toward Benagil and beyond. The full trail is 11.7 km but you can do a partial section. Completely free, stunning cliff scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: At Benagil Beach, join a budget kayak or stand-up paddleboard tour to see the famous Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil) — one of the most photographed spots in Portugal. Kayak rentals ~€15–20/person, much cheaper than boat tours (~€25–35). Alternatively, strong swimmers can swim into the cave from the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Benagil or walk back along the trail. Quiet evening at the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered: yogurt, fruit, and local bread from supermarket (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Benagil Beach — grilled sandwich or fresh orange juice (~€4–5). Pack extra water for the hike.
meals.dinner: A Ruína restaurant in Lagoa or cook a simple meal at accommodation. Fresh bread, canned sardines, local cheese, and wine from Pingo Doce (~€5)

day_by_day.notes: Start the hike early morning (before 9am) to avoid heat and crowds. Wear proper shoes — the trail has uneven cliff-edge terrain. Bring 2L of water minimum. The Benagil Cave is best visited at low tide.

day_by_day.morning: Lazy Sunday morning at Praia da Marinha. Swim, snorkel (bring or rent basic snorkel gear ~€5/day), and explore the rock pools at low tide. The waters are still warm in September (21–23°C).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sunday market in Lagoa (Mercado de Levante) if running — great for local produce, olives, almonds, figs, and handmade goods at low prices. Stock up on snacks and picnic supplies for the week.
day_by_day.evening: Wine tasting evening: visit Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar (5 km from Lagoa) — a boutique winery offering affordable tastings and vineyard walks. Book ahead; tastings from ~€10–15/person including 4–5 wines. Stunning sculpture garden on the estate.

meals.breakfast: Fresh pastries and coffee at a local padaria (bakery) in Lagoa (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach using market purchases — local figs, almonds, olives, bread, and cheese (~€4–5)
meals.dinner: Simple self-catered dinner at accommodation after the winery visit — local bread, cured meats, and a bottle of Quinta dos Vales wine purchased at the estate (~€6–8 total)

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales is one of the Algarve's top wine estates and very budget-friendly compared to Douro or Alentejo wineries. Pre-book tastings via their website. Taxi or rideshare from Lagoa is recommended (~€8 each way).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos — one of the Algarve's most beloved towns. Bus from Lagoa to Lagos (~30 min, €3). Explore the historic old town: walk the ancient city walls, visit Igreja de Santo António (church with stunning azulejo tiles, €2), and the adjacent Museu Municipal de Lagos (€2).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ponta da Piedade — extraordinary golden limestone sea stacks and grottos just south of Lagos town (free). Hire a rowing boat from the beach below to explore the sea caves (~€10–15/boat, split between 2–4 people). Alternatively, walk the cliff-top trail for free panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lagos' lively Rua 25 de Abril for budget tapas bars and cervejarias. Lagos has a great backpacker vibe with many affordable eateries.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and tosta mista at a café in Lagos old town (~€3)
meals.lunch: Mercado de Lagos (covered market) — fresh fruit, local snacks, and affordable food stalls (~€4–6)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos or O Camilo — look for fresh grilled fish of the day with salad and potatoes ~€10–12. Share a jug of local wine ~€4

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is very walkable. Ponta da Piedade is 2 km south of town — walk or take a tuk-tuk (~€5). The boat tours from the beach below the cliffs are much cheaper than organized tours from the marina.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Benagil again — this time explore the less-visited neighboring beaches: Praia do Carvalho (hidden tunnel beach) and Praia de Albandeira. All free, all stunning. Ideal for a peaceful morning swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Armação de Pêra (10 km east of Lagoa, local bus ~€2) — a large sandy beach popular with Portuguese families. Visit the small 17th-century chapel of Nossa Senhora da Rocha perched dramatically on a cliff headland (free). Walk the long beach promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Armação de Pêra has a small fishing harbor — watch the local fishermen bring in their catch in the late afternoon. Browse the fish market. Return to Lagoa for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — local bread, jam, and coffee (~€2)
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar at Praia de Albandeira or packed lunch from supermarket (~€4–5)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Zé in Armação de Pêra or back in Lagoa — grilled dourada (sea bream) with potatoes and salad ~€10–11

day_by_day.notes: The chapel at Nossa Senhora da Rocha is a hidden gem rarely mentioned in guidebooks. The cliff views are spectacular. September brings fewer crowds to Armação de Pêra, making it more enjoyable.

day_by_day.morning: Wine-focused morning: visit Adega do Cantor (Winery of the Singer) near Guia — founded by Cliff Richard, this is a well-regarded Algarve winery. Tours and tastings from ~€10. Book ahead. Located ~15 km from Lagoa (taxi or rideshare ~€12 each way).
day_by_day.afternoon: On the way back, stop at Guia village — famous for its piri-piri chicken restaurants. This is the birthplace of the famous Algarvian chicken. Spend the afternoon exploring the village and the nearby Zoomarine (skip if budget-conscious — entry ~€30, optional).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Praia da Marinha. Pick up a bottle of wine from your morning tasting and enjoy it on the cliffs at golden hour — one of the most memorable free experiences in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastel de nata at local café (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Guia piri-piri chicken — this is the budget splurge of the day. Restaurante Ramires in Guia is the most famous and authentic; half chicken with fries ~€8–10
meals.dinner: Light dinner: self-catered cheese, charcuterie, olives, and local bread with your winery wine (~€5)

day_by_day.notes: Adega do Cantor produces award-winning Algarve wines. The Vida Nova Rosé and Vida Nova Tinto are excellent value. Guia's piri-piri chicken is a must-eat cultural experience — do not miss it.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Albufeira — the Algarve's most famous resort town. Bus from Lagoa (~25 min, €2.50). Visit the old town (Albufeira Velha) — charming whitewashed streets, clifftop views, and the Praça Túnel tunnel leading to Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local bus or walk to Praia da Oura or Praia de Santa Eulália — beautiful, less crowded beaches east of Albufeira. Swim and relax. Explore the coastal walking paths.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Albufeira old town for the evening atmosphere. The Rua Cândido dos Reis (known as 'The Strip') is lively but touristy — stick to the old town for more authentic and affordable options. Bus back to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Café in Albufeira old town — galão (milky coffee) and croissant (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Restaurante O Penedo in Albufeira old town — prato do dia with soup, main, dessert, and drink ~€8–9
meals.dinner: A Ruína in Albufeira (iconic cliffside restaurant) — can be pricey; opt for the simpler grilled fish dishes ~€12–14, or eat cheaply at a tasca before heading back

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira is more commercialized than other Algarve towns but the old town retains charm. Avoid The Strip area for dining — prices are inflated. September crowds are manageable.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at Praia da Marinha. This is your last full beach day — savor it. Bring a book, snorkel, and a picnic. The beach is at its most magical in the soft September morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Lagoa's local market and artisan shops for souvenir shopping. Budget-friendly finds: local honey (~€4), almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos, ~€3–5/box), cork products (~€5–15), and local wine (~€4–8/bottle). All authentic Algarvian products.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell wine tasting dinner: cook a special self-catered meal at the accommodation or book a slightly nicer restaurant for a modest splurge. Toast to the trip with a bottle of Algarve wine.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at a local café — eggs, toast, ham, juice, and coffee (~€5–6)
meals.lunch: Picnic on Praia da Marinha — fresh baguette, local olives, cheese, and fruit from Lagoa market (~€5)
meals.dinner: Splurge dinner: Restaurante Casa da Lagoa or Bon Bon (Michelin-starred but has a more affordable lunch menu; for dinner, opt for Restaurante Muxama in Carvoeiro ~€15–18/person including wine)

day_by_day.notes: Dom Rodrigos (almond and egg-yolk sweets wrapped in foil) are the quintessential Algarve souvenir. Buy them from local bakeries rather than tourist shops for better prices and freshness.

day_by_day.morning: Final exploration: walk the full coastal cliff path from Praia da Marinha to Praia de Benagil one last time. Take photos, swim at a secluded cove, and enjoy the dramatic scenery you've come to love over the past two weeks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Portimão for last-minute shopping at the Aqua Portimão shopping center or the pedestrian streets. Pick up any remaining souvenirs. Portimão also has a good Saturday market near the riverfront.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Carvoeiro or Lagoa. Celebrate the end of a wonderful budget trip to the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — use up remaining groceries (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Grilled sardines at a beachside tasca in Portimão — sardines are the Algarve's iconic dish and extremely affordable (~€6–8 for a full plate with bread and salad)
meals.dinner: Tasca Bela Vista in Carvoeiro or similar local restaurant — cataplana de marisco (seafood cataplana) shared between two people ~€18–22 total, a worthy final splurge

day_by_day.notes: Grilled sardines (sardinhas grelhadas) are best eaten in September when the season is still active. Order them with local bread and a glass of house white wine for the full experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — pack bags and check out. Take one last walk to the clifftop above Praia da Marinha for a final view. Collect any stored luggage and arrange transfer to Faro Airport (Eva Bus from Lagoa ~€5, or shared taxi ~€15–20/person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for Faro Airport. Allow 1.5–2 hours travel time plus check-in. Browse the airport shops for any last-minute local products (Algarve wines and almond sweets available airside).
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry home memories of golden cliffs, crystal-clear Atlantic waters, and excellent Algarve wines.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão at a café in Lagoa before departure (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Airport café or bring packed snacks from supermarket (~€4–5)
meals.dinner: On the flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 13 days: Accommodation (pre-booked), Food ~€8–15/day, Transport ~€3–5/day local buses, Activities ~€5–10/day, Wine tastings ~€30–40 total for 2–3 sessions, Souvenirs ~€20–30. Total daily budget achievable at €30–40/person/day excluding accommodation.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage and arrange car rental (recommended for the Algarve).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive ~45 minutes from Faro to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa. Check in to Lagoa Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely first stroll along the Praia da Marinha clifftop trail to admire the iconic golden limestone arches and sea stacks. Short but stunning 1 km coastal walk.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the area with a relaxed dinner at a nearby local restaurant in Carvoeiro village (10 min drive). Explore the charming whitewashed streets and watch the sunset over Carvoeiro beach.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at Faro Airport café
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Faro Airport or a roadside café en route (pastel de nata and coffee ~€3–5)
meals.dinner: O Castelo Restaurant, Carvoeiro — mid-range seafood and grilled fish, expect €20–30 per person including wine

day_by_day.notes: Car rental is strongly recommended for the full 13 days to explore the Algarve coast freely. Book in advance for best rates. September weather is warm and sunny (~26°C), ideal for beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to Praia da Marinha beach — one of Portugal's most beautiful beaches. Arrive early (~9:30) before day-trippers. Swim in crystal-clear turquoise water, explore the sea caves accessible by foot at low tide, and photograph the dramatic rock formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 15 minutes to Benagil Cave — take a guided kayak or SUP tour from Praia de Benagil to enter the famous Algar de Benagil sea cave (book in advance, ~€20–25 per person). Alternatively, join a boat tour from Benagil beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Carvoeiro area for a wine-focused evening. Visit a local wine shop or wine bar to sample Algarve regional wines (Negra Mole and Aragonez varieties). Dinner at Restaurante Boneca, Carvoeiro.

meals.breakfast: Café da Marinha or hotel breakfast — croissant, fresh orange juice, coffee (~€6–8)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or light bites at Benagil beach café — sandwiches and local pastries (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Boneca, Carvoeiro — traditional Portuguese dishes, cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) ~€22–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil kayak/boat tour the evening before or online in advance. September is still busy — morning slots fill fast. Low tide is best for cave exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 30 minutes west to Portimão. Visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sunday, ~€3 other days) — an excellent converted fish-canning factory museum that tells the story of the Algarve's sardine industry and regional history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Rocha — a wide, golden sandy beach in Portimão with dramatic cliffs. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing. Walk the clifftop boardwalk for panoramic views of the Atlantic.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Portimão for dinner — the city is famous for its grilled sardines and riverside dining along the Arade River waterfront. Explore the lively marina area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or local café in Lagoa — toast, cheese, ham, fresh fruit (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Tasca do Celso, Portimão — local tasca (tavern) with daily specials, grilled fish, and cheap house wine (~€12–15 per person)
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré, Portimão riverside — grilled sardines, piri-piri chicken, local wine ~€18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Portimão hosts a famous Sardine Festival in August, but September still offers great sardine dining. The Arade riverfront is lively in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 20 minutes to Silves — the medieval Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€2.80 entry), walk the ancient ramparts, and explore the 13th-century Sé Cathedral below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wine tasting experience near Silves. Visit Quinta dos Vales winery (~15 minutes from Silves) — one of the Algarve's most acclaimed wineries. Book a guided vineyard tour and tasting session featuring their award-winning red and white wines (~€15–25 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Silves old town. Stroll along the Arade riverbank and enjoy the beautiful floodlit castle views after dark.

meals.breakfast: Café Central, Silves — fresh pastries, coffee, and orange juice (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Marisqueira Rui, Silves — famous local seafood restaurant, cataplana and grilled fish ~€20–28 per person
meals.dinner: Café Inglês, Silves — charming restaurant inside the castle walls, Portuguese cuisine with local wine ~€20–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales must be booked in advance (quinnadosvales.com). Silves is a highlight of the inland Algarve — very different from the coastal towns. The castle is stunning at sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 1 hour west to Sagres and Cape St. Vincent (Cabo de São Vicente) — the southwestern tip of continental Europe. Walk the dramatic clifftops, visit the lighthouse, and feel the raw Atlantic wind. An iconic, unmissable Algarve experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sagres town and Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry) — the historic fortress where Henry the Navigator reportedly planned Portugal's Age of Discovery. Walk the giant pebble compass (Rosa dos Ventos) inside the fortress grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back east (~1.5 hours) stopping in Lagos for dinner — one of the Algarve's most vibrant towns with a great nightlife and restaurant scene.

meals.breakfast: Early start — grab pastries and coffee from a Carvoeiro café before departing (~€5)
meals.lunch: A Sagres — simple café near the fortress, fresh fish sandwiches and soup (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Camilo, Lagos — stunning clifftop location, fresh seafood, panoramic views ~€25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Cape St. Vincent is windier and cooler than the rest of the Algarve — bring a light jacket. Sunsets here are legendary. Lagos is 30 minutes from Sagres and worth a dinner stop.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Lagos properly. Walk through the historic old town, visit the Igreja de Santo António (beautiful azulejo tile church, ~€2) and the adjacent Regional Museum. Stroll along the ancient city walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat tour from Lagos marina to explore the famous Ponta da Piedade grottos and sea caves (~€15–20 per person, 1–1.5 hours). The golden rock formations here are among the most spectacular in the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Lagos' lively Sunday evening atmosphere. Browse the local market stalls, have drinks at a rooftop bar, and enjoy dinner in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Mó Café, Lagos — excellent brunch spot, avocado toast, eggs, fresh juices (~€10–14)
meals.lunch: Picnic on Meia Praia beach (10 min from Lagos) — grab supplies from a local deli/market (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco, Lagos — cozy traditional Portuguese restaurant, bacalhau (salt cod) dishes and local wine ~€18–24 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ponta da Piedade boat tour at the Lagos marina on arrival. Sunday is busy — morning tours are easier to secure. Lagos has a very lively nightlife scene if you want to extend the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and beach day at Praia da Marinha. A mid-trip relaxation day — swim, snorkel (bring or rent a mask), and explore the rock pools and small caves accessible from the beach at low tide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 20 minutes to Armação de Pêra — visit the wide sandy beach, then explore the small fishermen's chapel (Nossa Senhora da Rocha) perched dramatically on a clifftop headland nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Wine and cheese evening — visit a local wine shop in Lagoa town (10 min drive) and pick up a selection of Algarve wines, local queijo (cheese), and presunto (cured ham) for a relaxed evening on your accommodation terrace.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café — full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, bread, cheese, ham (~€7–10)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia da Marinha — grilled chicken, salads, cold drinks (~€10–15)
meals.dinner: Self-catered terrace wine and cheese board from Lagoa market/wine shop (~€20–25 for two, excellent value)

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally slower-paced — 13 days is a long trip and a rest day prevents fatigue. Lagoa town has a good weekly market (check local schedule) and excellent wine shops specializing in Algarve DO wines.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 1 hour east to Faro. Explore the Faro Old Town (Cidade Velha) — walk through the 10th-century Arab walls, visit the Sé Cathedral and climb the bell tower for panoramic views (~€3.50), and browse the charming cobblestone streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a ferry from Faro marina to Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) or Ilha de Faro within the Ria Formosa Natural Park (~€5–8 return). Spend the afternoon on pristine, uncrowded barrier island beaches with calm lagoon waters.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Faro — explore the marina area and lively Rua de Santo António pedestrian street with its restaurants and bars.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Gardy, Faro — historic café, famous for pastries and coffee (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Tasca Dona Barca, Ilha Deserta — the only restaurant on the island, fresh fish and seafood in a remote setting (~€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dois Irmãos, Faro — one of Faro's oldest restaurants, traditional Algarvian cuisine ~€18–24 per person

day_by_day.notes: Ferries to the barrier islands run frequently from Faro marina. Ilha Deserta has one restaurant and pristine beaches — bring sunscreen. The Ria Formosa lagoon is a UNESCO-listed natural park and birdwatcher's paradise.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 45 minutes east to Tavira — widely considered the most beautiful town in the Algarve. Explore the Roman bridge, the castle ruins (free entry, great views), and the charming Igreja da Misericórdia with its Renaissance portal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the mini-train or ferry to Ilha de Tavira — a stunning barrier island beach within the Ria Formosa. The beach is long, wild, and relatively uncrowded in September. Perfect for swimming and a long beach walk.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Tavira old town — one of the most atmospheric evening settings in the Algarve, with riverside restaurants and beautiful tiled buildings lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: Café at your hotel or en route — coffee and pastries (~€5)
meals.lunch: Beach restaurant on Ilha de Tavira — grilled fish, salad, cold beer (~€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Quatro Águas, Tavira — riverside location, fresh seafood cataplana and local wines ~€22–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is a must-visit — its Moorish architecture, Roman bridge, and 37 churches make it the cultural gem of the Eastern Algarve. September is ideal — the summer crowds have thinned but weather is still perfect.

day_by_day.morning: Drive further east to Castro Marim — visit the impressive medieval castle and the 17th-century Forte de São Sebastião. The town sits on the Spanish border and offers sweeping views over the salt marshes of the Reserva Natural do Sapal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wine tasting in the eastern Algarve. Visit Herdade dos Pimenteiros or Monte da Casteleja winery near Vila Real de Santo António for a tasting of eastern Algarve wines (~€15–20 per person). Alternatively, drive to Vila Real de Santo António and take a short ferry across the Guadiana River to Ayamonte, Spain, for a cross-border afternoon stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back west (~1.5 hours to base) or stay overnight in Tavira for a more relaxed return. Dinner at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Café in Tavira or Castro Marim — coffee, toast, pastries (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Local tasca in Castro Marim — simple daily specials, soup, grilled meat or fish (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: If returning to base: Restaurante O Leão de Portimão or similar en route — grilled seafood ~€18–24 per person

day_by_day.notes: The eastern Algarve (Sotavento) has a different character — flatter, more tranquil, and less touristy than the western coast. The Guadiana River border crossing to Spain is a fun optional detour.

day_by_day.morning: Drive north into the Serra de Monchique mountains (~45 min from base). Visit the spa town of Caldas de Monchique — a beautiful valley village with thermal springs and a charming old quarter. Walk the forest trails and breathe the cooler mountain air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up to the summit of Fóia (902m) — the highest point in the Algarve. On clear days you can see both the Atlantic coast and the Spanish border. Explore the eucalyptus and pine forests. Visit Monchique town for local medronho (arbutus berry brandy) tasting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the coast for dinner. The contrast between the cool mountains and the warm coastal evening is a memorable Algarve experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or café — full breakfast before the mountain drive (~€7–10)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Central, Monchique — traditional mountain cuisine: smoked sausages, roast lamb, local bread and cheese (~€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Nortada, Carvoeiro — back on the coast, fresh seafood and cold local wine to end the day ~€20–26 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Serra de Monchique is a completely different ecosystem from the coast — lush, green, and cool. Don't miss buying medronho (the local firewater) and local smoked sausages (linguiça) from roadside stalls. A jacket is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Final full wine tasting day. Drive to Lagoa wine region — visit Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa, one of the oldest and most important wine cooperatives in the Algarve. Take a guided cellar tour and tasting of Lagoa DO wines including their famous fortified wines (~€10–15 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last beach afternoon at Praia de Carvoeiro or Praia do Paraíso — two beautiful beaches within 10 minutes of the hotel. Swim, relax, and soak in the last full afternoon of Algarve sunshine. Optional: rent a paddleboard or kayak from a beach vendor (~€15/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a special restaurant to celebrate the end of the trip. Choose a clifftop or seafront restaurant with views.

meals.breakfast: Slow hotel breakfast — enjoy the last leisurely morning (~€8–10)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery or a nearby café in Lagoa town (~€10–15)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon, Carvoeiro (Michelin-starred, splurge option ~€80–100 per person) OR Restaurante A Forja, Carvoeiro (excellent mid-range, ~€25–35 per person) — your choice based on budget mood

day_by_day.notes: Adega de Lagoa is open for visits — call ahead to confirm times (+351 282 342 181). The Lagoa region produces excellent table wines and unique fortified wines similar to sherry. September Saturdays can be busy on beaches — go mid-morning for best spots.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — pack up and take one last walk along the Praia da Marinha clifftop trail for a farewell view of the stunning coastline. Buy any last souvenirs: local wine, medronho, almond sweets (Dom Rodrigo), or carob products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Faro Airport (~45 minutes). Return rental car. Depart the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Travel home.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or café near the hotel — enjoy a last pastel de nata and bica (espresso) (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Airport café at Faro or a quick stop en route — light meal (~€10–15)
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before departure for car return and check-in at Faro Airport. Faro Airport has a good selection of shops for last-minute wine and food souvenirs (Algarve wines, local liqueurs, almond pastries). Check car return fuel policy before departure day.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning coastlines along the cliffside trail connecting Praia da Marinha to Benagil. Descend to hidden grottos, golden coves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters perfect for snorkeling and swimming. The dramatic limestone formations make this a bucket-list beach experience.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer from Faro Airport to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (~45 min). Settle into your luxury suite, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome drink on the terrace overlooking the Atlantic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely first stroll along the clifftops above Praia da Marinha to soak in the dramatic golden limestone formations and turquoise coves. Short 20-minute walk from the hotel — no strenuous activity, just orientation and awe.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo (15 min drive) — an acclaimed seafood restaurant set on the Arade River estuary. Order the grilled sea bass with local Algarve wines. Watch the sun dip behind the fortress walls of Ferragudo Castle.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport lounge
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the boutique hotel upon arrival — charcuterie, local cheeses, fresh bread, and chilled Vinho Verde arranged by the concierge
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste, Ferragudo — premium seafood tasting menu with local wine pairing (~€80–120 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Request the hotel concierge to pre-arrange private airport transfer and confirm dinner reservation at Sueste in advance. Ask for a sea-view room upgrade upon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim — embark on the iconic cliffside trail connecting Praia da Marinha to Benagil, one of the Algarve's most breathtaking coastal walks (~5.5 km one way). Stop at hidden coves and sea arches along the way. Swim at a secluded beach mid-trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat tour from Benagil Beach into the legendary Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil) — arrange through the hotel concierge for a private vessel. Continue along the coast to spot additional sea caves, arches, and grottoes inaccessible by land. Return to Praia da Marinha by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at the hotel terrace, then dinner at Vila Joya in Albufeira (25 min drive) — a two-Michelin-starred restaurant offering one of Portugal's finest tasting menus with exceptional wine pairings.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the boutique hotel — fresh pastries, local honey, Alentejo cheeses, smoked ham, eggs to order, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Light picnic basket prepared by the hotel — artisan sandwiches, fruit, sparkling water, and local pastries enjoyed on the cliffside trail or at a cove
meals.dinner: Vila Joya, Albufeira — Michelin two-star tasting menu (~€200–280 per person with wine pairing). Reserve weeks in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes and bring reef shoes for rocky cove swimming. Apply high-SPF sunscreen. The private boat tour should be booked 48 hours in advance through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure on Praia da Marinha — one of Portugal's most beautiful beaches. Arrive early to claim a prime spot on the golden sand between the sculpted rock formations. Swim in the crystal-clear water and explore the small sea arches accessible at low tide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wine tasting experience at Quinta dos Vales in Estômbar (~20 min drive) — a prestigious Algarve estate producing award-winning red and white wines. Enjoy a guided vineyard tour, barrel cellar visit, and premium tasting of 6–8 wines paired with local charcuterie and cheese. The estate also features impressive outdoor sculpture art.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Bon Bon Restaurant in Carvoeiro (10 min drive) — a Michelin-starred restaurant helmed by Chef Louis Anjos, offering creative modern Portuguese cuisine with an outstanding wine list.

meals.breakfast: Hotel gourmet breakfast — selection of Algarve pastries including carob cake and fig tarts, alongside eggs Benedict and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Wine and food pairing at Quinta dos Vales — charcuterie, regional cheeses, olives, and bread served alongside the tasting
meals.dinner: Bon Bon Restaurant, Carvoeiro — Michelin-starred tasting menu (~€120–160 per person with wine pairing)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Quinta dos Vales premium tasting experience in advance. Arrange a taxi or private driver for the evening to Bon Bon so both guests can enjoy the wine pairing without concern.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise kayaking tour along the Praia da Marinha coastline — paddle through sea arches, into hidden grottos, and along golden cliffs glowing in the early morning light. A guide leads you to spots inaccessible by foot or larger boat. Return by mid-morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Silves — the historic Moorish capital of the Algarve (25 min drive). Explore the magnificent red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves), the Gothic Cathedral, and the medieval old town. Browse artisan shops for handcrafted ceramics and leather goods.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Marisqueira Rui in Silves — a legendary seafood institution beloved by locals and food critics alike. Famous for its grilled percebes (barnacles), clams, and whole grilled fish. Pair with a chilled local white wine.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-kayak breakfast at the hotel — yogurt, granola, fresh fruit, and espresso
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Inglês in Silves — a charming restaurant within the castle walls offering grilled meats, salads, and regional dishes with panoramic views
meals.dinner: Marisqueira Rui, Silves — premium seafood feast (~€60–90 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The kayaking tour should be booked through the hotel concierge. Silves Castle is best visited in the afternoon when tour groups have thinned. Comfortable walking shoes recommended for cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning at Praia de Benagil — relax on the beach, swim, and snorkel in the gin-clear water. The beach is small and intimate, best enjoyed in the morning before it gets busy. Explore the shoreline rock pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private wine and olive oil tasting at Herdade dos Grous or a curated experience at a local Algarve producer arranged by the concierge — combining premium Alentejo wines (a short drive into the wine country) with estate-pressed olive oils, local honey, and regional produce. Alternatively, visit the Carvoeiro Boardwalk (Passadiço de Carvoeiro) and Algar Seco rock formations (10 min drive).
day_by_day.afternoon_alt: Algar Seco coastal walk in Carvoeiro — dramatic rock platforms, natural pools, and sea caves carved by the Atlantic. Visit the clifftop bar Boneca for a cocktail with a view.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at O Chambre in Portimão (20 min drive) — a sophisticated fine dining restaurant with an extensive Portuguese wine cellar and creative seasonal menu. Intimate ambiance ideal for a premium evening.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — smoked salmon, avocado, artisan breads, and a mimosa to start the weekend
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch at Praia de Benagil — fresh grilled fish, salads, and chilled rosé wine served at the beach restaurant
meals.dinner: O Chambre, Portimão — fine dining tasting menu (~€90–130 per person with wine)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday mornings at Benagil get busy by 10am — aim to arrive by 9am. Book dinner reservation at O Chambre in advance, especially for a Saturday evening.

day_by_day.morning: Spa morning at the hotel or a nearby luxury spa — indulge in a 90-minute couple's massage, hydrotherapy, and relaxation treatments. Many boutique hotels in the Marinha area partner with local spa facilities. Alternatively, enjoy a slow morning with breakfast in bed and pool time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Sagres and Cape St. Vincent (Cabo de São Vicente) — the southwestern tip of Europe (1 hour drive). Stand at the dramatic 75-metre cliffs where the Atlantic meets the horizon. Visit the 16th-century Sagres Fortress. Browse the artisan market near the lighthouse for handmade crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the Memmo Baleeira Hotel bar in Sagres — perched above the ocean with sweeping sunset views over Cape St. Vincent. Then dinner at A Sagres restaurant in Sagres village — fresh Atlantic seafood including percebes, spider crab, and grilled octopus.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast in bed or on the private terrace — full spread with champagne option
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mar à Vista in Vila do Bispo (near Sagres) — a rustic-chic seafood restaurant with ocean views and excellent grilled fish
meals.dinner: A Sagres, Sagres village — premium seafood dinner (~€55–80 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Cape St. Vincent can be very windy — bring a light jacket. The drive along the Vicentine Coast is spectacular. September sunsets at Sagres are legendary — arrive at the cape by 7pm to secure a viewing spot.

day_by_day.morning: Guided private snorkeling tour at Praia da Marinha and surrounding coves — explore underwater rock formations, sea fans, and abundant marine life with a certified marine biologist guide. Equipment provided. Suitable for all levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Loulé Market and old town (40 min drive) — Loulé hosts the Algarve's most authentic covered market (Mercado de Loulé), an Art Nouveau building filled with fresh produce, smoked meats, regional sweets, and artisan goods. Browse the Moorish-influenced old town and visit the castle ruins.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Gusto by Heinz Beck at Conrad Algarve in Quinta do Lago (35 min drive) — a Michelin-starred restaurant by world-renowned chef Heinz Beck, offering Italian-influenced fine dining with exceptional Portuguese wine selections and impeccable service.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — light pre-snorkel option: fruit, yogurt, and espresso
meals.lunch: Tasca do Zé Leiteiro in Loulé — a beloved local tasca serving traditional Algarve cataplana (seafood stew) and grilled fish. Authentic and excellent value
meals.dinner: Gusto by Heinz Beck, Conrad Algarve — Michelin-starred tasting menu (~€180–250 per person with wine pairing). Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The Loulé Market is best visited in the morning (opens 8am, winds down by 2pm) — consider adjusting the schedule to visit the market in the morning and do snorkeling in the afternoon if tides permit.

day_by_day.morning: Private catamaran sailing charter departing from Portimão Marina (20 min drive) — a full-morning luxury sail along the Algarve coast. Visit sea caves, snorkel in hidden bays, and enjoy on-board prosecco and snacks. The catamaran provides unmatched views of the cliffs from the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Portimão by early afternoon. Visit the Museu de Portimão — an award-winning museum built inside a former sardine canning factory, offering fascinating insights into the region's fishing heritage and history. Then stroll along the Portimão waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Taberna da Praça in Portimão — a refined modern Portuguese restaurant celebrating regional Algarve ingredients with a creative contemporary approach. Excellent natural wine list.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full gourmet spread before the sailing departure
meals.lunch: On-board the catamaran — premium catered lunch of fresh seafood, salads, local cheeses, fruit, and chilled wine served while anchored in a secluded cove
meals.dinner: Taberna da Praça, Portimão — modern Portuguese tasting menu (~€70–100 per person with wine)

day_by_day.notes: Book the private catamaran charter at least 3–4 days in advance. Request a vessel with a shaded deck and on-board catering for the full luxury experience. September seas are typically calm and ideal for sailing.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Praia da Rocha in Portimão — one of the Algarve's most iconic beaches, with its sweeping golden sands and dramatic rock formations. Walk the beach promenade and swim. Visit the Fortaleza de Santa Catarina (16th-century fortress) at the western end of the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium wine tasting road trip — visit Quinta da Tôr in Loulé (40 min drive), one of the Algarve's most acclaimed boutique wineries, for a private guided tasting of their award-winning Syrah and Viognier wines. The estate sits amid rolling hills with beautiful countryside views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a private in-room or terrace dinner arranged by the concierge — a chef's table experience with a local private chef preparing a traditional Algarve cataplana dinner using the freshest market ingredients, paired with wines selected during the day's tasting.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs any style, fresh pastries, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante O Faraó in Portimão — a well-regarded seafood restaurant near Praia da Rocha with excellent grilled fish and cataplana
meals.dinner: Private chef cataplana dinner at the boutique stay — arrange through concierge (~€150–200 per person including chef service and wine)

day_by_day.notes: The private chef dinner is a highlight experience — book 3–4 days in advance through the hotel. Specify dietary preferences. This is an excellent way to experience authentic Algarve cuisine in a luxurious private setting.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Ria Formosa Natural Park — depart early by private transfer to Faro (1 hour drive). Take a private boat tour through the lagoon system of Ria Formosa, visiting barrier islands, oyster beds, and flamingo habitats. Stop at Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) for a pristine, uncrowded beach experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lunch on Ilha Deserta at Restaurante Estaminé — the only restaurant on the island, serving exceptional fresh seafood and oysters harvested directly from the lagoon. After lunch, relax on the deserted Atlantic-facing beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Faro by late afternoon. Explore Faro's charming old town (Cidade Velha) — walk the Roman walls, visit the Gothic Cathedral and its bone chapel, and browse the marina. Dinner in Faro before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — packed efficiently before departure
meals.lunch: Restaurante Estaminé, Ilha Deserta — fresh oysters, grilled sea bream, and chilled local white wine in a spectacular setting (~€60–80 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Faz Gostos in Faro old town — a sophisticated restaurant in a historic mansion offering modern Algarve cuisine and an impressive wine cellar (~€70–100 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Ria Formosa boat tour and Ilha Deserta visit requires an early start — depart by 9am. September is an excellent month for birdwatching in Ria Formosa. Book the private boat through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning — sleep in, enjoy a long hotel breakfast, and spend time at the hotel pool or on the beach. This is a designated rest day after the full-day Ria Formosa excursion. Optional: book a 60-minute massage at a local spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming fishing village of Carvoeiro (10 min drive) — walk the boardwalk above the cliffs to Algar Seco, browse the village boutiques for ceramics and local art, and enjoy an afternoon coffee at a clifftop café. Visit the small but picturesque Carvoeiro beach.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style premium dinner at Restaurante O Castelo in Lagoa — a refined restaurant celebrating Algarve terroir with locally sourced ingredients, excellent regional wines, and warm, attentive service. A perfect encapsulation of Algarve fine dining.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury hotel breakfast — order everything on the menu, enjoy at leisure with a glass of cava
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Café Boneca at Algar Seco, Carvoeiro — sandwiches, salads, and cocktails on the clifftop terrace with Atlantic views
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo, Lagoa — premium regional tasting menu (~€80–110 per person with wine pairing)

day_by_day.notes: This slower day is intentionally designed as recovery and reflection time. Use the afternoon in Carvoeiro to purchase any artisan souvenirs — handmade tiles, local ceramics, and carob-based products make excellent gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Final coastal hike — the western section of the Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos) from Praia de Vale Centeanes to Praia da Marinha (3.5 km). A stunning cliffside walk with the most dramatic scenery in the central Algarve. Swim at the finish point at Praia da Marinha.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury beach afternoon at Praia da Marinha — arrange a private beach setup through the hotel (sun loungers, parasol, chilled champagne, and snack basket). Spend the afternoon swimming, reading, and simply savoring the final full day in the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at Ocean Restaurant at Vila Vita Parc in Porches (15 min drive) — a two-Michelin-starred restaurant by Chef Hans Neuner, widely regarded as one of the best restaurants in Portugal. A spectacular finale to the trip with a world-class tasting menu and cellar of over 1,000 Portuguese wines.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet hotel breakfast — treat yourself to the full spread one last time
meals.lunch: Champagne and gourmet snack basket on the private beach setup — smoked salmon blinis, oysters, charcuterie, and Algarve cheeses
meals.dinner: Ocean Restaurant, Vila Vita Parc — two-Michelin-star tasting menu (~€250–350 per person with premium wine pairing). Must be reserved weeks in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Ocean Restaurant at Vila Vita Parc is one of Portugal's most celebrated dining experiences — reserve as early as possible, ideally when booking the trip. Smart dress code required. This is the crown jewel dinner of the entire itinerary.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. Take one last walk along the Praia da Marinha cliffs to say goodbye to the Algarve coastline. Pack and check out. The hotel concierge arranges private transfer back to Faro Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure — private transfer to Faro Airport. Depending on flight time, enjoy a final coffee and pastel de nata at a café near the airport. Carry home bottles of Algarve wine, local honey, carob products, and artisan ceramics as edible and artisan souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of clifftop hikes, Atlantic swims, Michelin-starred dinners, and world-class wine in one of Europe's most beautiful coastal regions.

meals.breakfast: Final luxury hotel breakfast — order something special: eggs Benedict with smoked Algarve tuna, fresh pastries, and a farewell glass of cava
meals.lunch: Airport lounge or light meal at a Faro café — pastel de nata, bifana sandwich, and espresso
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before flight departure for the transfer and check-in. Ask the hotel to prepare a farewell gift bag — many boutique properties offer departing guests a bottle of local wine, homemade jam, or regional sweets. Confirm private transfer the evening before.
